notes: Deep sleep. The console can now power its chips down when it sleeps instead of just turning the screen off. New switch in Display and Sound, off by default: turn it on and the power button, the menu screen timeout and a game left alone for the auto sleep time all become a real sleep, the same kind the console does in Switch mode. Measured 89 mW asleep against 957 mW sitting in the menu, about 10 times better, so days on a charge instead of hours. Press the power button to bring it back, which takes a few seconds. Sleeping in a game saves a state first and loads it back when you wake, on the RetroArch consoles and 3DS; GameCube, Wii, PS2, DS and Wii U have no spare slot so they sleep frozen without one. Fixed: waking with the power button could immediately put the console back to sleep. Known issue: a high RAM overclock can stop the console waking up (one test console hung at 2300 MHz and was fine at stock). If that happens hold power for 12 seconds, then lower the overclock or turn deep sleep off.
